name: Anantara
intro: The set she wears once, and the set her daughter wears again. Anantara is our bridal line — heavy 22K harams, polki chokers and matched suites built to a weight that survives being handed down.
story: We begin every Anantara commission with a conversation and a photograph: the saree, the mandap, the grandmother whose necklace is being reworked. Nothing is drawn until we know what the piece has to live up to. Between eight and fourteen weeks, entirely by hand, in a workshop of eleven people.

name: Nilaya
tagline: Diamonds that come to work with you
intro: Certified stones in settings low enough to live under a sleeve. Nilaya is what we recommend when someone says they want diamonds but never take them off.
story: Every Nilaya setting is bezel or half-bezel, nothing that catches on wool. The stones are IGI-graded VS or better, because at this size clarity is what you actually notice across a table.
pieces: Studs · Pendants · Slim bands · Tennis bracelets

name: Vanaja
tagline: South Indian temple work, done properly
intro: Nakashi repoussé, granulated borders and antique-finished 22K. Vanaja draws on the temple jewellery of Tamil Nadu and Andhra, made by artisans who learned it from their fathers.
story: Antique finishing is a chemical patina, not a coating — it will not rub off on a blouse. Each Lakshmi and each peacock motif is struck from a hand-cut die, so no two pieces in the collection are quite identical.
pieces: Temple harams · Kasu malai · Vanki · Jhumkas

name: Solaire
intro: Solitaire rings and pendants built around a single certified diamond. We will show you four stones at four price points and explain honestly what separates them.
story: A Solaire appointment takes an hour. We put loose stones on a tray, hand you a loupe, and let you see the difference between VS1 and SI1 with your own eyes before anyone talks about money.
pieces: Solitaire rings · Halo settings · Bands · Pendants

name: Chandrika
tagline: Light gold for a lighter life
intro: Under six grams, mostly. Ear cuffs, threaders, thin chains and stacking bands for people who find traditional weight impractical.
story: The hardest jewellery to make is the lightest — there is nowhere for a bad joint to hide. Chandrika pieces are laser-welded rather than soldered, which is why a 1.8g chain survives a decade.
pieces: Ear cuffs · Threaders · Thin chains · Stacking bands

name: Kanaka
tagline: No stones. Nothing to date it.
intro: Plain 22K in the shapes that have not changed in fifty years — because they did not need to. Bangles, chains, studs and the mangalsutra your mother would recognise.
story: Kanaka is our best exchange value, because there is no stone weight to deduct. What you buy at 916 comes back at 916, at whatever the rate is that morning.
